findings.statement: idle I/O priority on the seal and merge threads takes the commit phase to at most 0.9x the baseline's without lifting seal or merge past 1.15x
findings.detail: commit phase 0.011s idle against 0.011s baseline (baseline vs idle-io: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.920, p=0.2298) -- within noise, not a result); seal 0.012s against 0.013s, merge 0.010s against 0.011s. The seal writes 64 MB while the commit path issues a barrier per batch on the same device; the idle class asks the block layer to serve the barrier first. Refuted with the phases unchanged means the host's scheduler ignores the class

findings.statement: idle I/O priority lifts ingest-to-routed by at least 1.05x
findings.detail: idle-io 500968 ops/s against baseline 506766 (idle-io vs baseline: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.989, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result); device bytes 9.2 against 9.2 MB. The commit phase is about a third of the window, so this needs the seal and merge not to slow down in exchange for what the barrier gains

findings.statement: spreading the segment writer's syncs every 4 MB takes the commit phase to at most 0.9x the baseline's without lifting the seal past 1.15x
findings.detail: commit phase 0.011s spread against 0.011s baseline (baseline vs spread-4mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.952, p=0.9362) -- within noise, not a result); seal 0.013s against 0.013s, merge 0.010s against 0.011s; ingest 515136 against 506766 ops/s (spread-4mb vs baseline: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.017, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result). Dirty pages leaving in 4 MB slices instead of one 64 MB flush at finish -- or more barriers from the seal contending with the commit path's, which is the refutation

findings.statement: the two levers compose: both together reach at least the better of the two on the commit phase
findings.detail: commit phase 0.011s with both against 0.011s for the better single lever (baseline vs both: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.978, p=0.8102) -- within noise, not a result); ingest 516262 ops/s against baseline 506766 (both vs baseline: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.019, p=0.2101) -- within noise, not a result)

notes: four arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, f49's shape: the f42 durable load with the drain (seal, join, partition) inside the timed window. baseline is the shipping configuration; idle-io sets IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE on the seal and merge threads; spread-4mb has the segment writer fdatasync every 4 MB as it streams blocks; both is both. Phases from the engine: commit is the WAL append and its fdatasync, seal and merge are where the committing thread waits for them
